title: Pubs in England and Wales will accept digital ID
seoTitle: Pubs to accept digital ID in England and Wales
subtitle: New rules allow establishments to accept digital identification apps alongside physical documents.
excerpt: Establishments in England and Wales can now use digital ID apps for age verification under the new regulations.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
New rules for age verification

Pubs located in England and Wales will be able to accept digital identity apps as a means of proving age. The measure is based on new rules introduced on a Tuesday, allowing these venues to validate customers' ages via digital tools directly on mobile devices.

According to the guidelines, digital identification apps will operate alongside traditional physical ID documents. This means businesses are authorised to use the digital format for the required checks while still retaining the option to verify physical documents.

The context of age verification

Age verification in commercial premises plays a crucial role in regulating the consumption of age‑restricted products. Around the world, retailers are legally responsible for ensuring their customers meet the stipulated age requirements. Historically, this verification has relied on presenting documents issued by official bodies, such as identity cards, passports or driver’s licences. Examining these physical records helps prevent violations and promotes a safe consumption environment.

Digital identification technology

With the rise of mobile technology, digitising personal documents has become a global focus for modernisation and consumer convenience. Digital identity systems are designed to provide security and data protection, ensuring personal information is shared only with the user’s consent. Adoption of these technologies by retailers reflects an effort to adapt to a society that increasingly relies on digital solutions for everyday tasks.

The shift from strictly physical methods to hybrid systems that combine physical and digital elements requires businesses to understand how the new tools work. Training staff to recognise and validate different proof formats is a common practice when new regulations are rolled out. In this way, commerce aims to balance swift customer service with strict compliance to legal standards, ensuring technological innovation does not compromise required compliance standards.

With information from BBC News.
